'''Sandip Trivedi''' ({{langx|hi|सन्दिप त्रिवेदी}}; born 1963) is an Indian [[theoretical physicist]] working at Tata Institute for Fundamental Research ([[TIFR]]) at Mumbai, India, where had been the director.<ref>{{cite news |title=Sandip Trivedi takes charge as TIFR director |url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/Sandip-Trivedi-takes-charge-as-TIFR-director/articleshow/47995537.cms |work=The Times of India |date= 9 July 2015 |access-date=8 March 2016 |author=Yogita Rao}}</ref> He is well known for his contributions to [[string theory]], in particular finding (along with [[Renata Kallosh]], [[Andrei Linde]], and [[Shamit Kachru]]) the first models of accelerated expansion of the universe in low energy supersymmetric string (see [[KKLT mechanism]]).<ref>{{cite journal|title=de Sitter Vacua in String Theory|journal=Physical Review D|volume=68|issue=4|article-number=046005|arxiv=hep-th/0301240|author=Kachru, Shamit|author2=Kallosh, Renata|author3=Linde, Andrei|author4=Trivedi, Sandip P.|year=2003|doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.68.046005|bibcode=2003PhRvD..68d6005K|s2cid=119482182}}</ref> His research areas include string theory, cosmology and particle physics. He is now member of program advisory board of International Center for Theoretical Sciences (ICTS). He is also the recipient of the [[Infosys Prize]] 2010 in the category of [[Outline of physical science|Physical Sciences]].<ref>[http://www.infosys-science-foundation.com/infosys-prize-2010-winners.html#physicalsciences Infosys Prize 2010 - Physical Sciences] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101117022339/http://www.infosys-science-foundation.com/infosys-prize-2010-winners.html |date=17 November 2010 }}</ref>

==Education==
He completed his [[Master of Science|master of science]] (Integrated) in physics from [[Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur|IIT Kanpur]] in 1985. He was awarded his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in 1990 from [[California Institute of Technology|Caltech]], [[Pasadena, California|Pasadena]], USA. Later he went on to work as a [[Postdoctoral research|post-doctoral]] [[research associate]] at [[Institute for Advanced Study|IAS]], [[Princeton University|Princeton]] until 1992.

==Awards==
He won the prestigious [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology|Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Award]] in the Physical Sciences in 2005. He was the recipient of the [[Infosys Prize]] 2010 in the category of Physical Sciences.<ref>[http://www.infosys-science-foundation.com/gallery.html Infosys Prize 2010 - Gallery] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101130195243/http://www.infosys-science-foundation.com/gallery.html |date=30 November 2010 }}</ref> He is also a recipient of the [[TWAS Prize]] in Physics in 2015.<ref name="Prizes and Awards">{{Cite web |url=http://twas.org/article/winners-2015-twas-prizes-announced |title=Prizes and Awards |date=2016 |publisher=[[The World Academy of Sciences]]}}</ref>
